facts.statement: The genus was named and described in 2013 by a team including Rongjun Chen, Wenjie Zheng, and others.
facts.quote: The specimen was described and named by Rongjun Chen, Wenjie Zheng, Yoichi Azuma, Masateru Shibata, Tianliang Lou, Qiang Jin and Xingsheng Jin in 2013.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen includes sacrodorsal and sacral vertebrae, ribs, a femur, phalanges, and numerous osteoderms.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, DYM F0136, consists of sacrodorsal vertebrae, sacral vertebrae, dorsal ribs, femur, pedal phalanges, partial Ilium fused to two sacral ribs, ossified tendons and numerous osteoderms.

facts.statement: The femur of Dongyangopelta measures 46 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The femur measures 46 cm (18.1 in) in length.

facts.statement: The pelvic shield consists of fused osteoderms arranged in a rosette pattern where central osteoderms are not fully ringed by smaller ones.
facts.quote: The pelvic shield is made up of numerous fused osteoderms that form a rosette pattern, with the central, larger osteoderms not being completely ringed by smaller osteoderms.

facts.statement: Osteoderms found on the body include thin triangular plates ranging from 10 to 35 cm in length, as well as domed and cone-shaped varieties.
facts.quote: Numerous other osteoderms are known from different parts of the body, including thin triangular plates that range in length from 10 to 35 cm (3.9 to 13.8 in), domed osteoderms and cone-shaped osteoderms.

facts.statement: Dongyangopelta is classified within the clade Nodosauridae based on the separation of the femoral head from the great trochanter.
facts.quote: Chen and colleagues (2013) assigned Dongyangopelta to the clade Nodosauridae, based on the femoral head being well separated from the great trochanter.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Dongyangopelta in a polytomy with Sauroplites and Taohelong at the base of Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis performed by Arbour and Currie (2015) recovered it within a polytomy with Sauroplites and Taohelong at the base of Nodosauridae.

facts.statement: Dongyangopelta lived during the Albian to Cenomanian stages, approximately 113.2 to 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Cenomanian (113.2 to 93.9 million years ago)
